title: CET Iasi employees hold spontaneous protest over wage indexation
seoTitle: Iasi CET employees protest over wages

tea.why: Employees are protesting because they have not received a 6.5% wage indexation despite meeting legal requirements under Ordinance 89.
tea.want: They demand the government approve a memorandum to authorize a 6.5% salary increase before the end of November.
tea.changed: Nov 26: Approximately 150 employees gathered at the company premises during shift changes to demand the wage increase.

summary: On November 26, 2026, approximately 150 employees of CET Iasi held a spontaneous protest at the company's premises in Iasi, Romania. Organised by the Energia Union, the action was prompted by the government's failure to approve a memorandum for a 6.5% wage indexation, which the employees claim they are legally entitled to under Ordinance 89. Union leader Sorin Turcu stated that this was the third protest on the issue and warned that if the memorandum is not approved during the government's final November meeting, the legal window for the increase will expire. Mayor Mihai Chirica noted that requests were previously submitted to the Ministry of Development and the Ministry of Finance. The protest took place during shift changes and did not disrupt the supply of thermal energy to the city.
demands: Approval of the 6.5% wage indexation memorandum
response: Mayor Mihai Chirica stated that requests for the indexation were submitted to the Ministry of Development and the Ministry of Finance but have not yet been approved. He expressed hope that the government would resolve the issue during its meeting on November 26.

updates.text: Approximately 150 employees gathered at the CET Iasi facility to protest the lack of a 6.5% wage increase.
